Berdasarkan data OSINT Shodan & Censys, ada LEBIH DARI 20.000 website dan subdomain berakhiran .go.id yang berjalan di atas PHP! Dari kementerian pusat, dinas provinsi, pemkab, pemkot, sampai layanan publik daerah.

Masalah terbesarnya:
Mayoritas web pemerintah di daerah masih memakai PHP versi lama/EOL (PHP 5.6, PHP 7.x, PHP 8.0/8.1) yang TIDAK MENDAPATKAN PATCH RESMI dari dua celah kritis RCE (CVE-2026-109618 & 109619) dengan skor keparahan sempurna CVSS 10.0!

Tool 'PHP2Shell' sudah bocor, dan serangan bot scanner massal menyapu internet dalam hitungan menit. Jika tidak ada instruksi terpusat, puluhan ribu web instansi yang menyimpan data kependudukan masyarakat sangat rentan dieksekusi dari jarak jauh tanpa perlu login!

Panggilan terbuka untuk Kemkomdigi & BSSN:
1. Terbitkan Security Advisory Nasional segera untuk seluruh pengelola server .go.id.
2. Gerakkan Gov-CSIRT di setiap daerah untuk mitigasi dan patching.
3. Instruksikan penutupan fungsi rentan di php.ini (`disable_functions = exec,system,shell_exec,passthru`) sebagai langkah darurat pertama!

Jangan sampai kita baru bertindak setelah data masyarakat bocor lagi! Tag pihak terkait dan share video ini agar segera ada langkah konkret! 📢

When it was first adopted, vibe coding was supposed to embody the sort of care-free optimism that was running in AI circles at the time, high off the possibilities of the tech. AI models had become so powerful that you could build an app using the same conversational language that you deploy while confiding in ChatGPT.

But the “vibes” are different now. Programmers were quickly forced to grapple with the new reality that AI coding tools brought to their profession. Now that everyone’s using AI to churn out code, you have to crank out even more work to keep up and meet your boss’s quota. It may be more “efficient” — and even that’s contested, since someone needs to do the hard work of verifying all that AI pablum — but it hasn’t exactly made people’s jobs easier.

In sum, vibe coding has gone from a novelty to something viewed as a necessary evil, or worse, as an object of suspicion. It’s no longer something to brag about. A recent tweet making the rounds in tech circles perhaps encapsulates this shift, joking about using the term “cuck coding” instead of vibe coding “because you just sit in a chair and watch.” Even posters on r/ClaudeCoding found the humor in it.

As vulgar as the term sounds, maybe “cuck coding” is indeed the term that more accurately reflects what’s actually going on. You watch and burn … lots of tokens.
